title: OTel span-loss journal (user scratch)
content:
Quick running journal / scratchpad for the span loss incident affecting OTEL pipeline (observed Nov 7 2025-ish, recurring). Purpose: capture commands tried, raw error snippets, immediate hypotheses, quick queries to quantify impact, and short-term mitigations. This is messy by design.

Summary / symptom summary:
- Around 2025-11-07 03:18 UTC we saw a sudden ~60–75% drop in span ingestion for the hosted-api service as seen in metrics: spans_ingested_per_minute. Traces were incomplete: child spans present but parent spans missing in many traces (looked like parent id stripped or export failed).
- Logs from OTEL collector showed occasional ResourceExhausted / message size errors and repeated "retrying export" lines.
- Fluent forwarder metrics show increased queue_push_backpressure and fluentd posted "client connection closed with pending bytes" errors.

What I pulled so far (commands / queries) - run these on the cluster / logging workspace:
- kubectl -n telemetry get pods | grep collector
- kubectl -n telemetry logs otel-collector-5f9d -c otel-collector --since=2h | sed -n '1,400p' | grep -iE "error|drop|exhaust|retry|failed"
- kubectl -n telemetry exec -it otel-collector-5f9d -c otel-collector -- sh -c 'ps aux | grep collector'
- kubectl -n telemetry exec -it otel-collector-5f9d -c otel-collector -- sh -c 'ls -l /var/run/otel; du -h /var/log/collector || true'
- gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.cluster_name="prod-telemetry" AND "Received message larger than max"' --limit 50 --project=redwood-telemetry
- BigQuery span rates (run in telemetry dataset):
  SELECT
    TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(received_at, MINUTE) as minute,
    count(1) as spans
  FROM telemetry.spans_v2
  WHERE service_name = 'hosted-api'
    AND received_at BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2025-11-07 02:30:00 UTC') AND TIMESTAMP('2025-11-07 04:30:00 UTC')
  GROUP BY minute ORDER BY minute DESC LIMIT 240;

Raw / notable log snippets I copied:
- "exporter/otlptracesgrpc: error: failed to export spans: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = Received message larger than max (120371 > 104857)"
- "processor/batch: dropped 153 spans due to buffer overflow"
- "level=error msg=\"failed to enqueue span; queue full\" service=otel-collector"
- "fluentd: client closed connection with 1.2MB pending (max 1MB)"
- HTTP exporter stacktrace: "proto: message too large; cannot marshal"

Immediate hypotheses (unordered):
1) New client instrumentation or feature started attaching very large attributes (embedding vectors / base64 payloads) which blow past the gRPC max message size and cause the gRPC exporter to reject whole batches. If exporter errors, collector may drop those spans or trigger backpressure.
2) Batch processor config (batch_size, send_batch_max_size, timeout) changed in the last config push — causing larger-than-allowed batches. The gRPC exporter max_receive_message_length/default may be lower than the batch sizes we produce.
3) Resource exhaustion: memory/cpu/cgroup throttling on collector pods leading to intermittent inability to process buffered spans -> queue overflow -> dropped spans.
4) Upstream fluentd/fluent-bit forwarder started failing due to TLS renegotiation or chunking changes; logs show pending bytes and closed connections. That can create holes in log/span ingestion as well.
5) A recent model rollout that attached large prompt/embedding attributes (seen on hosted-api traces) created exceptionally large span payloads — specifically check attributes named 'embedding_vector', 'payload_blob', 'prompt_text' length.

What I checked and immediate findings:
- Checked last config commit in k8s ConfigMap: telemetry/collector-config map was updated 2025-11-07 03:10 UTC by ci/cd pipeline (see git SHAs in linked_artifacts). The change included batch processor tweaks (batch_size from 100 to 500, timeout from 5s to 2s). That matches spike time.
- grep through recent deployments: found PR#847 in gitops that altered otel batch processor.
- Correlate: span size histogram shows a long tail starting Nov 7 with 0.5% of spans > 500KB (previously < 0.05%).
- No obvious node OOMs around that time; CPU and memory metrics for collector pods were elevated but not critical.

Quick repro / experiments to run (low-risk):
- Roll back the batch processor config to previous values (batch_size 100, timeout 5s) in a staging collector and see if large message errors disappear.
- Temporarily set exporters.otlp.max_recv_message_size to 4MB (or set to a value slightly above observed max) in staging to see if ResourceExhausted stops. Note: don't increase arbitrarily in prod without audit.
- Add a per-span attr size limiter in instrumentation (hosted-api) for a short period (truncate 'prompt_text' to 8k chars and drop 'embedding_vector' attribute) and check rate.
- Run a targeted query to find top attr keys by serialized size: stored in BigQuery config snapshot table or run a histogram on length(attributes_json).

Safe short-term mitigations tried (and results):
- Rolled collector config back in prod at 2025-11-07 04:02 UTC -> span ingestion partially recovered (~+30%) but still not full; indicates multiple factors.
- Deployed a temporary rate-limit filter on hosted-api instrumentation to drop large spans at source (saw immediate drop in error logs). That reduced ResourceExhausted logs but also reduced trace fidelity (expected).
- Restarted collector pods (kubectl rollout restart) -> short window where backlog cleared but errors reappeared after ~20m.

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Add per-attribute size enforcement in server SDK wrappers (truncate or remove very large attributes automatically and emit a warning metric).
- Tune batch processor to use lower batch_size for services with variable attribute sizes; consider dynamic batching based on avg serialized span size.
- Increase OTLP exporter max_recv_message_size + gRPC settings system-wide (with caution) and track memory impact.
- Reject oversized spans early with explicit metric and a helpful reason string (for upstream devs to fix).
- Add CI gate to prevent instrumentation PRs from adding huge attributes blindly (lint/size check).

Notes for follow-up / who to ping:
- Ping @Liam Chen to check PR#847 and rationale behind batch_size bump.
- Ping hosted-api team (SRE and SDK owners) to ask about recent telemetry changes: check PRs that added 'embedding_vector' attribute.
- File JIRA (JIRA-TELE-324) to track permanent fix (attr-truncation + exporter tuning).

Open questions / things I still need:
- Need a precise histogram of span serialized sizes across last 7 days (BigQuery query).
- Are any other services showing similar tail of large spans, or isolated to hosted-api?
- Confirm whether exporter settings in collector config include max_recv_message_size and whether gRPC server/client defaults differ between versions.
- Check if any older collector version had different marshalling behavior that masked this issue.

Short TODOs (next 48h):
- [ ] Run serialized-size histogram query and paste results here.
- [ ] Recreate change in staging with batch_size=500 to see exact error reproduction steps (Liam).
- [ ] Push attr-truncation shim to hosted-api canary and monitor spans for 1hour (Saira to deploy).
- [ ] Draft brief postmortem outline if impact persists.

Random checklist / misc notes for myself:
- If we increase max_recv_message_size, update exporter docs and add alert for high memory on collector pods.
- Look at protobuf versions between exporter client and server — mismatch can produce strange behavior.
- Consider switching heavy attribute blobs to separate artifact store (S3) and only put a short ref/id in span attributes.

Appendix: helper commands snippets (pasteable)
- grep of collector logs for dropped spans:
  kubectl -n telemetry logs otel-collector-5f9d -c otel-collector --since=6h | grep -i "drop" | sed -n '1,200p'
- query for large attributes (BigQuery example):
  SELECT service_name, count(1) as cnt, approx_top_count(attr_key, 20) as top_keys
  FROM (
    SELECT service_name, key as attr_key, length(value) as vlen
    FROM telemetry.spans_attributes
    WHERE received_at > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
  )
  WHERE vlen > 10000
  GROUP BY service_name
  ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 50;

End of messy notes. Will keep appending findings here as I run experiments.

Evelyn
